title.narrative: Activity under preparation Green Energy in Kenya

description.narrative: The proposed Action will support Kenya advancing towards an effective climate resilient low-carbon economy and society, by facilitating investments in green and reliable energy. The action contributes to the implementation of the Global Gateway strategy and the TEI on Green Deal, building on ongoing and planned Team Europe actions in the energy sector in Kenya.Kenya set ambitious targets to reach universal electricity access and a 100% green electricity grid by 2030. These targets are currently challenged by a significant electricity demand increase, with a peak of 2,43 GW recorded in December 2025, driven by economic expansion, increased industrial and commercial activity, rapid urbanization, and higher household consumption. To cope with excess demand, Kenya is implementing load-shedding with localized, controlled power reductions to protect the system from overloading, as well as importing electricity from Ethiopia and Uganda. Experts project the upward trend for electricity demand will continue, forecasting a 6.5% annual increase between 2025 and 2027. New renewable electricity generation is therefore highly needed and prioritized in the Government of Kenya¿s (GoK) agenda, along with network upgrade and development, and expanding baseload (hydro, geothermal) and storage capacity, crucial to allow the absorption of more generation from intermittent renewable sources.Considering that significant programmes are underway for the expansion and modernization of the distribution and transmission network, with funding from Team Europe and the World Bank, the core of the action is mainly focused on supporting the expansion of domestic electricity generation and storage capacity from renewable sources suchas wind, hydropower, geothermal and/or solar. Furthermore, a 2021 moratorium on new Power Purchase Agreements (PPAs) stalled private sector generation projects for nearly five years, contributing to delays in capacity expansion and weakening investor confidence. Although recently lifted, the legal and fiscal frameworks governing Public Private Partnerships (PPPs) and Independent Power Producer (IPPs) remain under consolidation. The delay has created a generation gap relative to peak demand growth and reduced investor appetite. This provides an opportunity to offer a structured European investment package that supports a pipeline of power generation investments, and which is aligned with Kenya¿s ambition to remain a regional renewable hub.To complement investments, and in line with the Global Gateway 360-degree approach, the action will also target soft support to investments, potentially beyond power generation, in the form of design and implementation of inclusive energy policies and regulations to an enabling environment for energy entrepreneurship, technical assistance to executive agencies, studies and project preparation, to ensure a strategic positioning of Team Europe.
